main_body: Dark green ground patch (gothic style) tiled with small tuft/stone motifs on a flat dark green base; terrain tile, not a standing object
top_band: none - flat ground texture, no standing volume
evidence: The candidate is a seamless ground patch viewed from above, with small repeating tufts and dark patches. It has no standing body, so the 3/4 top/front contract does not apply. No side faces are drawn and no elevation view is present. It is a plausible terrain tile.

style.evidence: The ground is a dark green base with 4 close value steps (base, lighter tuft, dark shadow, deep patch) plus sparse reddish dots. The motif repeats on a regular grid, so the pattern reads as mechanical and the texture is low in contrast. There are no large flat areas, but the per-tile variety is lower than the Beodeul grass and paving references, which carry more clumps, highlights, and stone shading. Dark tuft shapes with hard rectangular shadow bars look blocky. It is acceptable but a bit thinner than the reference, so I fail it on strictness.
